prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, surveys point to an interesting tension in travel among young people in Japan, especially young men.

Many want trips that feel more personal and less rushed. But the trips being measured are still short.

In one 2025 survey, men aged 29 and under showed strong interest in solo travel and travel that helps them deepen a hobby. The figures were about 25% and a similar share.

Another survey found a similar wish for freedom. About 90% of Gen Z respondents aged 19 to 25 wanted free time during an overseas tour. Most of those respondents wanted at least half a day.

The desire also appears when people imagine having more time. In a survey, the most common answer was “about one week” when people were asked how long they would travel with a one-month vacation. About one in four chose that answer.

Yet an autumn survey from the same research center measured much shorter stays among people planning a trip: an average of 1.8 nights, with a median of about two nights.

That is the central tension. The preferred shape of travel seems to be becoming more open and self-directed, while actual stays have not become long in the same way. The 2025 Tourism White Paper says longer stays are still a policy task. It also says many people see travel as something to do when they have enough time and money.

The pattern is not the same for everyone. Among women aged 29 and under, about 45% were interested in visiting famous tourist spots. So the story is not a complete change from sightseeing to slow travel. It is a mixed, uneven shift.

【Point One】
Slow travel does not have to mean adding many nights. It can also mean taking back part of a fixed schedule. The wish for at least half a day without tour plans is a concrete sign of that. For travel planners, the immediate question may be how much open time a short trip offers, not only how long it lasts.

【Point Two】
Young travelers are not one market. For men under 29, solo and hobby-focused trips stand out. Another 2025 survey also found solo travel was the top travel arrangement for men aged 18 to 29. For women under 29, food travel led at about 52%, while famous spots remained high at about 45%. This points to parallel offers, not one replacement model. Solo travel alone does not prove a long stay.

point_one.reasoning: 半日以上の自由時間という具体的な調査結果を、宿泊日数を増やさずに短い旅行の中で自由度を高めるという解釈に発展させている。旅行商品では総日数だけでなく、固定予定にどれだけ余白を設けるかが重要になるという実務的示唆もあり、Full Storyの単なる言い換えではない。

point_two.reasoning: 男女別の旅行目的に加えて、男性ではソロ旅行が首位、女性では食旅行が約52%という追加データを示し、若者向け市場を単一モデルで捉えるべきでないと具体化している。ソロ志向をそのまま長期滞在志向と解釈できないという整理も、記事の中心的な緊張関係への新しい注意を加えている。
